decls.classical: the Dixmier–Malliavin factorization theorem. Every compactly supported Bruhat test on the idele class group is a finite sum of convolutions of two such tests, for the Tamagawa Haar measure. J. Dixmier and P. Malliavin, *Factorisations de fonctions et de vecteurs indéfiniment différentiables*, Bull. Sci. Math. The library proves the case of tests of one angular character (`spectralHomogeneousTest_convolution_factorization` in §10.3). The structural quotient and zero extension reduce this to factorization on the elementary Lie group.

decls.doc:
Paper: Theorem 10.4.2.1, p. 459, at orders `0 ≤ s ≤ 1`. Every compactly supported Bruhat
test acts on the strip quotient by a Hilbert–Schmidt operator.
Reconstruction: The paper does not state this. It is the estimate of the argument posted on
#7405 for the whole range. After the Mellin transform, each angular component of the quotient
is `D_s ⊖ V` for an equivalent norm `∫_{∂S} |F|² + ∬_S |F'|² (α − |σ|)^{1−s}` on the strip
`S = {|Re z| < α}`, where `V` is the space of functions that vanish at the zeros in the open
strip. That identification is `spectralStripJet_commonKernel`; at `s ≤ 1` no boundary jet
survives. A Carleson formula with a positive measure for finite Blaschke products gives an
orthonormal basis `B_{n−1} g_n` of `D_s ⊖ V`. A positivity bound for the normalized kernels
`g_n`, uniform in the measure, gives `‖Φ g_n‖² ≪ (1 + (Im ρ_n)²)^{−M}`, and the count of zeros
with multiplicity makes the sum converge.
Gap: Not proved in Lean. The argument is posted on #7405 as mathematics and was checked there
by other contributors, not by Lean; the library has no Hardy or Dirichlet-type space of the
strip in which to carry it out. Nothing in the Lean outside this file uses this statement.
decls.gap: Not proved in Lean. The argument is posted on #7405 as mathematics and was checked there by other contributors, not by Lean; the library has no Hardy or Dirichlet-type space of the strip in which to carry it out. Nothing in the Lean outside this file uses this statement.

decls.doc:
Paper: Theorem 10.4.3.5(2), p. 472. For each zero `z` of the strip, let `R_z` be the
finite-rank operator `v ↦ ∑ₘ f_{z,m}(q v) • P^geom_a(A(φ)(S_a x_{z,m}))` on the Sobolev space,
summed over the jets kept at `z`; here `q` is the quotient map and `S_a` its isometric section.
The finite sums of the `R_z`, over arbitrary finite sets of zeros, are bounded in trace norm.
Reconstruction: The paper gives no estimate for the geometric component (p. 472). This is the
geometric analogue of the bound that `spectralStripConvolution_traceCauchy` obtains for the
quotient sums; with `traceClass_blockSums_tails_of_bddAbove` it implies
`spectralStripGeometricKernel_cauchy`. It asks for more than that statement: summability of
the blocks in every order, where the theorem needs convergence along its rectangles only. It
is equivalent to the summability, for every compact
operator `U`, of `z ↦ ∑ₘ f_{z,m}(q(U(P^geom_a(A(φ)(S_a x_{z,m})))))`, by uniform boundedness.
Gap: No bound is known for the geometric output of convolution on the biorthogonal vectors,
that is, for the part of `A(φ)(S_a x_{z,m})` outside the spectral subspace; the bound
(10.4.2.34) on p. 464 does not give one. The statement implies that `P^geom_a ∘ A(φ) ∘ P^spec_a`
is nuclear on the Sobolev space, which is not known either. Nothing in the Lean uses this statement, and it is not
known how it connects with the rest of the proof in Lean; in the paper it is used on pp. 471–474.
decls.gap: No bound is known for the geometric output of convolution on the biorthogonal vectors, that is, for the part of `A(φ)(S_a x_{z,m})` outside the spectral subspace; the bound (10.4.2.34) on p. 464 does not give one. The statement implies that `P^geom_a ∘ A(φ) ∘ P^spec_a` is nuclear on the Sobolev space, which is not known either. Nothing in the Lean uses this statement, and it is not known how it connects with the rest of the proof in Lean; in the paper it is used on pp. 471–474.

Gap: Theorem 10.4.2.8 gives a cutoff trace limit. Identifying it with this

decls.classical: R. Meyer, *On a representation of the idele class group related to primes and zeros of L-functions*, Duke Math. J. 127 (2005), arXiv:math/0311468 (page numbers are those of the preprint), Corollary 4.17, p. 34, and Lemma 4.20, p. 36, at α = 1: the direction from bounds on the Mellin transforms to bounded classes, in the cases that Lean does not prove. For a sequence of tests whose θ-classes have one conductor level and lie in one Fréchet subspace of the θ-quotient: if the Mellin transforms of the θ-functions of the tests, and of their additive Fourier transforms, are bounded on every line of real part greater than one (supported on a finitely generated subgroup of the discrete factor of the dual, with every polynomial weight bounded uniformly in the index), then the θ-classes form a bounded set.
decls.doc:
Classical input: R. Meyer, *On a representation of the idele class group related to
primes and zeros of L-functions*, Duke Math. J. 127 (2005), arXiv:math/0311468 (page numbers
are those of the preprint), Corollary 4.17, p. 34, and Lemma 4.20, p. 36, at α = 1: the
direction from bounds on the Mellin transforms to bounded classes, in the cases that Lean does
not prove.
For a sequence of tests whose θ-classes have one conductor level and lie in one Fréchet
subspace of the θ-quotient: if the Mellin transforms of the θ-functions of the tests, and of
their additive Fourier transforms, are bounded on every line of real part greater than one
(supported on a finitely generated subgroup of the discrete factor of the dual, with every
polynomial weight bounded uniformly in the index), then the θ-classes form a bounded set.
Deviation: This is what remains of the criterion `sLocalMellinSchwartzBounds_meyer`, which is
proved from it below. Proved in Lean, and excluded here by hypothesis: the case in which the
classes span a finite-dimensional space (`hS`), and the case in which they are given by even
real Schwartz profiles (`hreal`; it covers ℚ with no finite place). The other direction of the
criterion is proved in Lean as well (`sLocalMellinSchwartzBounds_meyer_general_forward`). The
hypotheses `hk`, `hM` and `hm` follow from the bounds and are proved before this statement is
applied. The bounds are written without derivatives, which is equivalent
(`sLocalMellinSchwartzBounds_meyer_zeroth_iff`), and the conclusion is boundedness in the
quotient, which is equivalent to representatives in one bounded set
(`sLocalMellinSchwartzBounds_meyer_lift_iff_quotient_bounded`).
The paper states its results for bornological spaces and in the variable of the idele
classes. Writing them for this library is the project's work and is not proved in Lean:
that the bounded sets of the Schwartz–Bruhat space here are the paper's, that the kernel of
the S-unit sum is the closed span the paper divides by, the normalizations of the Fourier
transform and of the Haar measures, and the seminorms on the dual group. The integrator and
an independent reviewer checked these steps against the paper for the whole criterion (#7346);
no specialist in the paper's framework has.

Paper: Theorem 7.3.3.4, p. 360, with the coefficient change on p. 349.
At repeated primary poles of an infinite-order character, keep only strict closest
approaches to one among distinct centers through squared height.
Only infinitely many such centers with unbounded inverse distances remain. A repeated
pole also gives a character-kernel element of infinite order modulo finite units.
No number field of degree at most two has such a pole.
Reconstruction: The paper does not state this. It is what remains of the project's formulation
`sLocalPWOrbital_bases_bounded_interpolation_laurent_other_prime_shift` of the bound that the
change of coefficients on p. 349 needs, after the cases that Lean proves (#7413), and it is not
known whether it is what the author intends.
Gap: For these separated record centers the phases of the Hecke character still need a
polynomial inhomogeneous lower bound (Theorem 7.3.3.4, p. 360, using p. 349).
decls.gap: For these separated record centers the phases of the Hecke character still need a polynomial inhomogeneous lower bound (Theorem 7.3.3.4, p. 360, using p. 349).

Paper: Proposition 10.2.2.2, pp. 446–447. For each choice of basepoints the real
interval (1/2, 1) contains only finitely many distinct multiple zeros of the family.
Reconstruction: This tests only ordinate zero. A different choice of basepoint may move
one prescribed ordinate to zero independently in each norm-one component.
Gap: Compactness gives finiteness for each character on this segment. Finiteness across
components for every choice of basepoints is open.
decls.gap: Compactness gives finiteness for each character on this segment. Finiteness across components for every choice of basepoints is open.

multiple-zero line strictly to the right of the centre has a representative at bounded
height. The height bound may depend on the character.
Reconstruction: This isolates the single-character part of the strip margin.
Gap: Discreteness on compact rectangles does not control new abscissae at increasing heights.
decls.gap: Discreteness on compact rectangles does not control new abscissae at increasing heights.

decls.doc:
Paper: Proposition 10.2.2.2, pp. 446–447.
One integer bounds the multiplicity of every zero of every chosen completed Hecke
L-function: all components of the norm-one dual, all real parts and all ordinates at once.
This is the half of `spectralStripJet_order_and_margin_locally_finite_multiple_zeros` that
bounds the orders of the strip jets.
Reconstruction: The paper does not state this. It is the project's formulation of the bound on
the orders that the norm integral of Proposition 10.2.2.2, p. 447, needs, and it is not known
whether it is what the author intends.
Gap: The known bounds for the multiplicity of a zero grow with its height and with the
conductor. Over `ℚ` this statement contains a height-independent bound for the multiplicities
of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function, which is open, also on the Riemann hypothesis
(report on #7220). The statement that all zeros lie on the critical line does not supply it.
decls.gap: The known bounds for the multiplicity of a zero grow with its height and with the conductor. The statement that all zeros lie on the critical line does not supply it.

Paper: Theorem 10.3.2.1(1), pp. 453–455. After inserting any fixed compact
operator on the biorthogonal vectors, the scalar traces of the individual zero
blocks are summable. The jets at each zero are summed before testing summability.
The estimates for (10.3.2.7) involve only Mellin derivatives and give no bound for these
pairings with a compact operator. A summable majorant for the absolute block
traces, allowed to depend on the operator and test, would suffice.
Reconstruction: The paper does not state this. It is the project's formulation of what the
trace-norm estimates of Theorems 10.3.1.1(1) and 10.3.2.1(1) need, and it is not known whether
it is what the author intends.
Gap: The estimates on pp. 454–455 bound Mellin derivatives only. No bound for the block traces
against an arbitrary compact operator, allowing clusters of zeros, is supplied or known to us.
decls.gap: The estimates on pp. 454–455 bound Mellin derivatives only. No bound for the block traces against an arbitrary compact operator, allowing clusters of zeros, is supplied or known to us.

decls.doc:
Paper: Theorem 10.3.2.1(1), pp. 453–455, after (10.3.2.7). For a fixed test,
discard the output directions of finitely many jets. The positive square root of
the remaining Gram operator should have uniformly small finite diagonal sums.
By `_hb` the Riesz vectors span densely, so the complementary projections tend strongly to
zero and compress any fixed finite-rank rectangle to zero in trace norm. In a trace-norm
Cauchy tail, contractivity bounds each later compressed trace norm, and hence each finite
diagonal sum, by the fixed rectangle's compressed trace norm plus the tail error.
Gap: The scalar Mellin estimates on p. 455 do not control this sum for an
individual rectangle, in particular when its boundary separates nearby zeros.
decls.gap: The scalar Mellin estimates on p. 455 do not control this sum for an individual rectangle, in particular when its boundary separates nearby zeros.

decls.classical: the number of distinct critical-line zeta ordinates up to height T, divided by T, is unbounded. This follows from a positive proportion of distinct critical-line zeros (Selberg 1942) and the Riemann–von Mangoldt count. Not a statement of the paper and not a gap in it: a known theorem of which this project has no formal proof. It is the arithmetic input for the refutation of (10.3.1.18), p. 451, which is proved from it by name.
